incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure (energy, defense, healthcare, IT, finance)
incidents.vector: MOIS-directed hackers breached employee email accounts and exfiltrated data from US critical-infrastructure firms and government offices (including the Department of Labor, FERC, and UN organizations) since late 2023.
incidents.impact: US Treasury sanctioned six Iranian nationals and DOJ indicted four for extensive compromises of US critical infrastructure and financially motivated theft; some members also targeted Iranian firms and stole cryptocurrency for personal gain.

incidents.vector: Cyber intrusion into operational technology at a small-scale UK power plant, reportedly by the same actors who breached US water utilities; reports indicate an unsecured programmable logic controller (PLC) was involved.
incidents.impact: The plant shut down operations for four days last month; no customers lost power and the wider grid was unaffected, but officials called it a major escalation from earlier water-utility targeting.

incidents.vector: Unauthenticated remote code execution via CVE-2026-73570, an input-sanitization flaw in Zimbra SNMP notification processing (enabled by default), triggered by crafted SMTP requests.
incidents.impact: CISA added the bug to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after active exploitation; federal agencies were given a three-day deadline to patch. Compromised mail servers expose calendars, contacts, and attachments useful for follow-on attacks.

incidents.victim: Mobile banking, e-wallet, and crypto app users
incidents.vector: ToxicPanda 2.0 Android banking Trojan distributed via AWS-hosted buckets; abuses Accessibility Services to enable Wireless Debugging/ADB for privilege escalation and uses a lock-screen overlay to steal credentials.
incidents.impact: Expanded from 16 to 349 banking, e-wallet, and cryptocurrency apps with 167 remote commands, achieving full device compromise and persistence, putting both consumer finances and enterprise resources on infected devices at risk.

incidents.vector: Data breach at French telecom SFR disclosed last month; intrusion method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Personal data of more than 2.1 million customers stolen, including names, postal addresses, phone numbers, and contract/connection details; some records also exposed IP addresses and equipment details.

incidents.victim: Owners of DoFun Android car head units
incidents.vector: Attackers abused the legitimate TWCore updater on Chinese-made DoFun head units to silently push a malicious downloader (JarService), with no driver interaction required.
incidents.impact: First documented malware infection of car head units via a purpose-built attack; infected units are turned into reverse proxies for a botnet, attributed to the MoYu Group linked to the BadBox operation. Vendor says it has fixed the issues.

incidents.victim: Internet-facing web servers (government, education, media, tech, gaming)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — Chinese-speaking (SEO fraud, data theft)
incidents.vector: UAT-10147 exploited publicly disclosed one-day vulnerabilities (Zimbra, Nacos, AjaxPro) for RCE, then used agentic AI to automate exploitation, reconnaissance, and payload generation, deploying BadIIS and the new cross-platform SPECTRE implant with BYOVD EDR-killing and a Linux rootkit.
incidents.impact: Compromised servers across Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada, and Vietnam for SEO fraud and data theft; a target list of ~170,000 URLs was recovered. Talos assesses AI integration lets the actor scale complex intrusions with less expertise.

incidents.victim: Academics, diplomats, and think-tank staff (Europe and US)
incidents.vector: Three suspected Russian clusters (tied to the group formerly tracked as APT29) abuse legitimate authentication flows — app-password phishing, OAuth and device-code phishing, and WhatsApp device linking — impersonating the US State Department and event organizers.
incidents.impact: Persistent, adaptive social-engineering campaigns compromise personal and enterprise accounts of individuals of interest to Russia, bypassing two-factor authentication; one cluster also records victim audio/video after WhatsApp device linking.

incidents.vector: Attackers breached Apollo's cloud systems using a social engineering attack at the start of July, part of a broader wave targeting US investment and Wall Street firms.
incidents.impact: Customer data stolen; the firm confirmed the breach in a letter to the California attorney general. The campaign against financial-sector targets is continuing.

incidents.vector: Attacker exploited the protocol's anti-theft defenses to trick the platform into issuing unwanted loans; investigators believe an AI tool was used to chain six smaller unrelated bugs.
incidents.impact: Roughly $1.7 million in crypto assets stolen from the protocol.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure using Siemens S7 PLCs
incidents.industry: Critical manufacturing, energy, water, chemical, food/agriculture
incidents.vector: Threat actors use internet scanning services to find exposed or poorly protected Siemens S7 PLCs, then deploy AI-generated Python scripts using the snap7 library to gain read/write access via the S7comm protocol while masquerading as legitimate monitoring tools.
incidents.impact: NSA/CISA/FBI warn of active reconnaissance and capability development against US Siemens S7 installations, assessed as pre-positioning for potential operational effects; unauthorized PLC access could disrupt industrial processes, cause safety incidents, or damage equipment.

incidents.victim: Universities, companies, and government agencies (US and allied)
incidents.vector: Mabna Institute hackers ran spearphishing campaigns using stolen credentials to access professor accounts across 144 US and 178 foreign universities, plus private companies, government agencies, and NGOs.
incidents.impact: DOJ unsealed a superseding indictment charging 17 Iranians; the campaign (2013-2017) stole at least 31.5 terabytes of academic data and intellectual property, with State offering up to $10 million rewards for five defendants.

incidents.victim: Organizations running Fortinet, Sophos, and MSSQL services
incidents.vector: Large-scale internet-wide password spraying ("FortiBleed") using a curated password list against internet-exposed edge services, followed by privilege escalation, device configuration extraction, and offline credential cracking to establish persistent admin access.
incidents.impact: An initial access broker on a Russian-language cybercrime forum claimed responsibility and offered harvested credentials for sale; harvested credentials are recycled to compromise additional devices. Unit 42 blocked related login attempts in customer telemetry.

incidents.industry: Healthcare, education, legal, insurance, technology, manufacturing
incidents.vector: Medusa ransomware-as-a-service affiliates gain access via phishing and by rapidly exploiting unpatched vulnerabilities (including ScreenConnect, Fortinet EMS, Fortra GoAnywhere, and BeyondTrust CVEs), often within 24 hours of disclosure, then use double extortion.
incidents.impact: FBI/CISA/HHS updated their joint advisory: Medusa actors have impacted over 500 victims as of April 2026, encrypting data and threatening to leak exfiltrated data unless ransoms are paid.

incidents.vector: North Korean IT workers (tracked as PurpleDelta), likely operating from China, used 22+ fabricated personas with AI-generated photos, custom ChatGPT assistants, and forged identity documents to secure remote jobs, aided by real-time AI interview tools.
incidents.impact: Operators were likely actively employed at ten or more organizations, presenting an ongoing insider threat; earnings are funneled to fund the DPRK regime, with observed overlap with malware-deploying clusters raising supply-chain risk.

incidents.vector: The ChainDrop npm worm modified package manifests with a malicious preinstall script that launched an obfuscated payload; a hidden script read live process memory on GitHub Actions runners to steal OIDC tokens and secrets, using stolen tokens to self-propagate.
incidents.impact: Over 400 packages including widely used libraries were infected, with malware also backdooring local developer tools (VS Code, Claude Code) and managing C2 via Ethereum blockchain transactions while preserving legitimate package functionality.

incidents.vector: SynkLoader malware delivered via phishing from an attacker-registered Microsoft 365 tenant impersonating IT support, with the installer hosted on official Microsoft Azure storage; it runs in-memory PowerShell/Python with fake Microsoft DLLs and a fake Windows lock screen ("PhishLocker") to steal passwords.
incidents.impact: Newly discovered multitool combining a system profiler, persistence, RAT, desktop takeover, and reverse proxy; a network-sizing module suggests it is being staged for follow-on ransomware by a ransomware group or initial access broker.

incidents.vector: An actor using the handle "TheHatman" claimed to have exfiltrated employee data from organizations' Microsoft Entra tenants, allegedly using compromised credentials obtained via MFA fatigue and password spraying (unverified by Unit 42).
incidents.impact: From Aug 1-17, the actor advertised sensitive employee information from several high-profile enterprises for sale across multiple cybercrime forums; the specific intrusion vector remains unverified.

incidents.victim: Elderly victims in New York and New Jersey
incidents.vector: Scammers impersonating law enforcement or government officials convinced elderly victims to empty accounts and buy gold or gift cards; a US-based money mule collected the funds and routed them to India.
incidents.impact: At least nine victims lost a total of $7.5 million; money mule Jay Sunilbharthi Goswami was charged, fled the US, and was arrested by Canadian authorities awaiting extradition. He faces up to 20 years.

incidents.victim: Consumers on payment and shopping platforms
incidents.vector: The undocumented "JWR" phishing framework impersonates checkout and login pages of Shopify, PayPal, Apple, Klarna, and banks, using an AES-encrypted WebSocket to let operators steer victim sessions live and stream keystrokes; delivered via SMS lures impersonating toll authorities and postal/courier services.
incidents.impact: Harvests full payment card data, credentials, 2FA codes, SSNs, and passport/ID images across 44 phishing pages in real time. Talos observed a live campaign across Southeast Asia and the Middle East; assessed as a variant of the "Outsider" PhaaS platform.

incidents.vector: North Korean espionage actors breached South Korea's Presidential Office in February as part of a broader campaign; intrusion methods have not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: The campaign racked up more than 100 victims by April, including universities, police departments, news agencies, and hospitals. South Korean authorities are still investigating.
